_note: Narration script for the Falls module (CPP-045-AO v1.0, CTL-003, CTL-010, CPPRO-001). Lee voice on eleven_v4, one take, short conversational sentences. The prompt sent to ElevenLabs starts with the [calmly] tag and spells EOC as "E O C", FROP as "Frop", CRU as "C R U", PCR as "P C R"; captions use the text here.

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Falls.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: Why falls matter
sentences: Falls are one of our most common jobs.
And you're often the first health professional in that person's home.
That's a chance to see how they're really managing.
One fall is a strong warning sign for the next one.

lines.head: The long lie
sentences: Ask how long they were on the floor.
More than an hour is a long lie.
It can mean muscle damage, pneumonia, pressure sores, dehydration and hypothermia.
And it's linked to higher mortality in older people.

lines.head: Assess first
sentences: Start with basic care.
A full set of obs, and the full story of the fall.
Treat anything urgent you find.
Then plan the lift. Call for support if you need more hands or gear.

lines.head: Mobility check
sentences: Before you lift, check their mobility.
Can they lift each leg to touch your hand?
Can they bridge, lift their head, and roll?
If not, they're unlikely to stand safely.
Skip it with low blood pressure, a possible spinal injury, active chest pain, or significant confusion.
And if they start to fall, don't catch them. Protect their head.

lines.head: Who goes to hospital?
sentences: Transport if there's a medical cause for the fall.
Or an injury.
Or other clinical or social concerns.
Or they need more tests or treatment.
And transport anyone on anticoagulants.

lines.head: The FROP screen
sentences: Staying home? Do the FROP falls screen.
Three questions, each scored nought to three.
Falls in the last year, counting today's.
How much help they need around the house.
And how steady they are when they walk and turn.
Nought to three is low risk. Four to nine is high risk.

lines.head: Refer
sentences: High risk needs an urgent referral. Low risk, consider a non-urgent one.
In the country, that's the Country Referral Unit.
Email the CRU form, or phone them during business hours.
Get the patient's consent first.

lines.head: Pressure injury
sentences: After a long lie, screen for pressure injury with the Braden score.
A low score means higher risk.
Twelve or below is high risk. Arrange a review with their doctor.
And if there's already a pressure injury, make sure there's a plan.

lines.head: Before you leave
sentences: Leaving someone at home? Consult the EOC Clinician.
Make sure they're supervised.
Tell them when to call again.
And leave a falls handout if you've got one.
